question: Where do the game processes' CPU time and a game thread's wall time go in training at 256x8 on the Mac's GPU, on main after the zone input pruning (673076c)?
code: 673076c, run from a git archive copy with its compiled engine module; PyTorch 2.14.0
machine: Apple M4 Max, 10 performance and 4 efficiency cores, 36 GB

commands.driver:
#!/bin/bash
# Where the game processes' CPU time goes in training at 256x8 on the Mac's GPU, on main 673076c:
# one training iteration of 126 eleven-round games in 7 processes of 18, compiled layers, with every
# game thread's CPU time charged to the engine call it is in and native stack samples of four game processes.
set -u
cd REPO
OUT=$PWD/tmp/engine-profile-2026-11-19
LEARNING=(--calendar-rounds 11 --complete-episodes --batches 1 --transitions-per-batch 20000 --simulations 64
          --max-depth 16 --hidden-dim 256 --message-layers 8 --batch-size 32 --epochs 525 --replay-capacity 8000
          --sample-fraction 0.05 --seed 20261119 --neural-device mps --no-continuous --compiled-forward
          --episode-workers 7 --games-per-process 18 --parallel-envs 126)
echo "== $(date '+%F %T') start" >> $OUT/driver.log
(cd $OUT/code && env -u MallocNanoZone .venv/bin/python tools/profile_game_process_cpu.py --output $OUT/game.json \
  --profile mac --control-dir $OUT/game-control --run-dir $OUT/game-run --seconds 3600 \
  --sample-at 180,420,660,900 --sample-seconds 20 -- "${LEARNING[@]}" > $OUT/game.log 2>&1) &
profiler=$!
.venv/bin/python tools/log_process_load.py record --pid $profiler --output $OUT/game-load.jsonl > /dev/null 2>&1 &
logger=$!
wait $profiler
echo "== $(date '+%F %T') end, exit $?" >> $OUT/driver.log
wait $logger
echo "== $(date '+%F %T') done" >> $OUT/driver.log
